comment: router-update and router-recovery are installed to /usr/libexec/minimalrouter/bootstrap,
outside the A/B slot. cmd/router-update/runtime_layout.go requires a candidate release to
carry byte-identical copies of them before it will activate an A/B slot, because a binary
that survives rollback cannot itself be rolled back by moving a symlink.
bootstrap_baseline_ref names the release those bytes are unchanged since. Appliances running
that baseline (or any later release sharing it) can take this build as a dashboard web update.
Appliances older than it need the full signed distribution installer once.
scripts/ci/bootstrap-compatibility.sh proves the claim by building both refs with the same
toolchain and deterministic flags. When bootstrap source genuinely changes, update this file
in the same pull request and document the one-time installer step - never relax the
byte-identity check to make a release pass.
bootstrap_change_reason: Both bootstrap binaries changed in v0.1.7, for two deliberate reasons. router-recovery links internal/config, and internal/config/validation.go changed after v0.1.6 (firewall source and lease-time validator fixes) - the recovery console must validate exactly like the release it ships with. router-update shrank: GitHub release discovery and payload preparation moved from internal/firmware to internal/release, which router-update does not import, so the binary that decides activations no longer carries HTTP and archive code and future changes to release discovery cannot break bootstrap identity. Appliances running v0.1.6 therefore take v0.1.7 through the full signed distribution installer once.
deterministic_bootstrap_note: Releases up to and including v0.1.6 were built without -buildvcs=false, so Go stamped the
commit hash and derived module version into the bootstrap binaries. Two such releases can
never be byte-identical, which made web updates between published releases impossible for a
reason unrelated to compatibility: v0.1.5 and v0.1.6 differ only in vcs.revision, vcs.time and
the module version string. From the first release built with GO_BOOTSTRAP_BUILD_FLAGS, the
bytes depend on bootstrap source and toolchain only.
